paragraphs.title: A Rebellious People and the Demonstration of Exile

easy.explanation: The Lord calls them a rebellious house.
easy.q: How is the house to which Ezekiel is sent described?

easy.explanation: He was told to prepare stuff for removing.
easy.q: What was Ezekiel commanded to prepare?

easy.explanation: He dug through the wall and carried his belongings out.
easy.q: What did Ezekiel do through the wall?

answers: So they might consider what they saw
So they could learn to build walls
So they could prepare a feast
medium.explanation: The Lord said, “it may be they will consider,” though they were rebellious.
medium.q: Why was Ezekiel to perform these actions in the sight of the people?

medium.explanation: His actions represented the people removing and going into captivity.
medium.q: What did Ezekiel’s belongings and departure represent?

answers: The dim time between day and night
medium.explanation: Ezekiel carried his belongings in the twilight, or dim evening light.
medium.q: What does the KJV word “twilight” describe in this passage?

answers: They have eyes and ears, but do not see or hear
They see and hear well but cannot speak
They speak much but cannot walk
challenge.explanation: They have eyes to see and ears to hear, yet they refuse to perceive.
challenge.q: What contrast is emphasized about the people?

answers: To show that he was asleep
To picture a secret and uncertain departure
To protect him from the sun
challenge.explanation: Covering his face helped represent the dark and uncertain character of exile.
challenge.q: Why was Ezekiel told to cover his face?

answers: He merely reported an old event
He watched the exile from a distance
He was set as a sign to the house of Israel
challenge.explanation: The Lord said, “I have set thee for a sign unto the house of Israel.”
challenge.q: What role did Ezekiel have in this action?

paragraphs.title: The Prince and the Coming Exile

easy.explanation: The burden concerned the prince in Jerusalem and the house of Israel.
The Lord said He would bring him to Babylon, to the land of the Chaldeans.
easy.q: Where would the prince be brought?

answers: They would be scattered in every direction
easy.explanation: The Lord would scatter those around him toward every wind.
easy.q: What would happen to those around the prince?

answers: In the twilight and through the wall
medium.explanation: He would bear his burden in the twilight and go through the wall.
medium.q: How would the prince attempt to leave?

medium.explanation: The net represented the prince being taken in the Lord’s snare.
medium.q: What would happen when the Lord spread His net upon the prince?

answers: A trap used to catch someone
medium.explanation: The prince would be captured in the Lord’s trap.
medium.q: In this context, what does “snare” mean?

answers: Ezekiel’s action gives an early picture of the prince’s fate
Ezekiel’s action describes only Ezekiel’s life
challenge.explanation: The Lord declared, “like as I have done, so shall it be done unto them.”
challenge.q: What connection is made between Ezekiel’s action and the prince’s fate?

answers: He would be brought to Babylon and die there
He would hide in another city
challenge.explanation: He would be brought to Babylon, yet would not see it, though he would die there.
challenge.q: Why would the prince not see the land?

answers: To rule in place of the prince
To declare their abominations among the heathen
challenge.explanation: The survivors would declare their abominations among the nations where they came.
challenge.q: Why would a few men be left from the people?

paragraphs.title: Anxiety, Destruction, and a Desolate Land

easy.explanation: He was told to eat his bread with quaking.
easy.q: How was Ezekiel told to eat his bread?

easy.explanation: He was to drink with trembling and with carefulness.
easy.q: How was Ezekiel to drink his water?

answers: They would be filled with people
easy.explanation: The Lord said the inhabited cities would be laid waste.
easy.q: What would happen to the inhabited cities?

medium.explanation: His fearful actions pictured the coming distress.
medium.q: What did Ezekiel’s trembling eating and drinking represent?

medium.explanation: The land would become desolate because of the violence of its inhabitants.
medium.q: What would violence in the land lead to?

medium.explanation: The people would drink their water with astonishment, meaning fear and shock.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “astonishment” describe?

challenge.explanation: The passage moves from fearful behavior to ruined cities and a desolate land.
challenge.q: What is the main sequence described in the passage?

answers: The land was about to be emptied and ruined
There were not enough eating vessels
The people were preparing for a feast
challenge.explanation: Their behavior pictured the distress accompanying the land’s desolation.
challenge.q: Why would the people eat bread with carefulness and drink water with astonishment?

answers: The cities would be laid waste and the land desolate
The cities would become strong and the land full
challenge.explanation: The Lord explicitly says that the cities would be laid waste and the land desolate.
challenge.q: What overall result is stated at the end of the section?

paragraphs.title: The End of the Saying About Delayed Visions

answers: The days are prolonged, and every vision faileth
The vision has already come to pass
easy.explanation: They said, “The days are prolonged, and every vision faileth.”
easy.q: What proverb did the people use about the days and the vision?

easy.explanation: The Lord said, “The days are at hand.”
easy.q: What did the Lord say about the days?

easy.explanation: The Lord declared that the vision’s effect would occur.
easy.q: What would happen to the effect of every vision?

answers: To end the claim that the vision was delayed or had failed
To encourage the people to forget the prophecy
To show that the vision was unimportant
medium.explanation: He rejected the proverb and announced that the days were at hand.
medium.q: Why did the Lord make the proverb cease?

answers: The people claimed nearness, but the Lord announced distance
The people claimed distance, but the Lord announced nearness
Both said that everything was finished
medium.explanation: The people pushed the prophecy into the future, while the Lord said the days were at hand.
medium.q: What change appears between the people’s claim and the Lord’s word?

answers: The time for the prophecy to be fulfilled is near
The appointed time has already ended
medium.explanation: The phrase means that fulfillment was approaching.
medium.q: What does “the days are at hand” mean?

answers: The prophecy will be fulfilled soon
Every vision concerns only the past
challenge.explanation: The Lord says the days are at hand and the vision will take effect.
challenge.q: What is the main message about prophecy in this passage?

answers: God’s word does not fail but comes near to fulfillment
The people had already forgotten the land
The vision concerned only other nations
challenge.explanation: The Lord declares that the vision will take effect rather than fail.
challenge.q: Why does the Lord’s word contradict “every vision faileth”?

answers: Ending the proverb confirms that fulfillment is near
Ending the proverb delays the prophecy further
Ending the proverb cancels the Lord’s word
challenge.explanation: The Lord replaces the saying about delay with an announcement of approaching fulfillment.
challenge.q: What is the connection between ending the proverb and the days being at hand?

paragraphs.title: False Visions and the Authority of God’s Word

easy.explanation: The Lord said there would be no more any vain vision.
easy.q: What would no longer be found in the house of Israel?

easy.explanation: He said, “the word that I shall speak shall come to pass.”
easy.q: What did the Lord say would happen to the word He spoke?

answers: Push it into the distant future
easy.explanation: They said the vision was for many days to come and for times far off.
easy.q: What were the people trying to do to the vision?

answers: A vain vision fails, but God’s word comes to pass
God’s word is farther away than a vain vision
medium.explanation: The passage rejects vain visions and emphasizes that God’s spoken word will be fulfilled.
medium.q: What is the difference between a vain vision and God’s word?

answers: To announce that its fulfillment would no longer be delayed
To send the people farther from their land
medium.explanation: He declared that the word He had spoken would be done without further delay.
medium.q: Why did the Lord emphasize that His word would not be prolonged?

medium.explanation: It refers to deceptive predictions that falsely reassure or flatter the hearers.
medium.q: What does “flattering divination” mean in this context?

answers: It depends on the people’s wishes
God speaks it, and it comes to pass
challenge.explanation: The Lord says that the word He speaks shall come to pass.
challenge.q: What authority of God’s word is emphasized?

answers: It was for many days to come and far-off times
It had already been completely fulfilled
It had nothing to do with them
challenge.explanation: They claimed that the vision concerned a distant future.
challenge.q: What was the house of Israel claiming about the timing of the vision?

answers: He confirms that the vision is far away
He says that some of His words will fail
He ends the delay and promises that His word will be done
challenge.explanation: The Lord declares that none of His words will be prolonged and that what He has spoken shall be done.
challenge.q: How does the Lord answer the claim of delay?
